g.text: Do components correspond to cross-layer virtual attention heads?

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: A virtual head is a PAIR of heads whose circuits multiply through the residual stream. Scoring that (Elhage et al.) recovers the textbook

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: previous-token → induction circuit at 2.05× chance, and specifically on K-composition — so the measure is sound. Head pairs that share a

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: component nonetheless compose at chance. What components DO capture is heads playing the same role in different layers: 360 of 4096 are

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: significantly induction-enriched, and co-owned cross-layer pairs are 14% closer in behaviour than random pairs.
